locator: I q.105 a.5 co.: all agents act in virtue of God Himself
interpretation: 'And thus all agents act in virtue of God Himself: and therefore He is the cause of action in every agent'; the third way adds that God 'moves things to operate', applying their forms and powers to operation as a workman applies the axe, besides giving and preserving those forms (also ad 3: God 'applies them to act'). Read as: every created agent, whatever else is true of it, acts only as moved to act by God. Aquinas also rejects the view that God alone acts (created things have their proper operation, ad 1 and ad 2), so the reading is not occasionalism. As evidence on q.2 a.3: on this text no created mover is a first mover of its series in its own right, which is what the strong per se reading requires and the weaker reading leaves open. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
